---
title: "Prototype"
---

The **Prototype** pattern creates new objects by **cloning** existing ones. Instead of building objects from scratch, you copy a prototype and modify it as needed. This is especially useful when object creation is expensive or when you want to avoid coupling to concrete classes.

## Problem

Imagine you're building a graphic editor. Users can create shapes (circles, rectangles) and need to duplicate them. The naive approach requires knowing all the fields of each shape class to copy them manually.

### Example

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Manual Copying"
        O[Original Circle]
        C[Copy Code]
        N[New Circle]
        O -->|"read x, y"| C
        O -->|"read radius"| C
        O -->|"read color"| C
        O -->|"private fields?"| Q[???]
        C --> N
    end

    style Q fill:#faa,stroke:#333
    style C fill:#f96,stroke:#333
```

**Problems with manual copying:**

- Must know all fields of the object (including private ones)
- Client code is coupled to concrete classes
- If the class changes, all copy code must be updated
- Some objects have circular references or complex state

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
class Circle:
    def __init__(self, x: int, y: int, radius: int, color: str):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.radius = radius
        self.color = color
        self._internal_id = id(self)  # Private field!

class Rectangle:
    def __init__(self, x: int, y: int, width: int, height: int, color: str):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.color = color
        self._internal_id = id(self)  # Private field!

def copy_shape(shape):
    # Must know the concrete type!
    if isinstance(shape, Circle):
        # Must know all fields
        copy = Circle(shape.x, shape.y, shape.radius, shape.color)
        # Can't copy _internal_id - it's private!
        return copy
    elif isinstance(shape, Rectangle):
        copy = Rectangle(shape.x, shape.y, shape.width, shape.height, shape.color)
        return copy
    raise TypeError("Unknown shape type")
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
public class Circle
{
    public int X { get; set; }
    public int Y { get; set; }
    public int Radius { get; set; }
    public string Color { get; set; }
    private readonly Guid _internalId = Guid.NewGuid();  // Private field!
}

public class Rectangle
{
    public int X { get; set; }
    public int Y { get; set; }
    public int Width { get; set; }
    public int Height { get; set; }
    public string Color { get; set; }
    private readonly Guid _internalId = Guid.NewGuid();  // Private field!
}

public static class ShapeCopier
{
    // Must know the concrete type!
    public static object CopyShape(object shape)
    {
        if (shape is Circle c)
        {
            // Must know all fields
            return new Circle { X = c.X, Y = c.Y, Radius = c.Radius, Color = c.Color };
            // Can't copy _internalId - it's private!
        }
        if (shape is Rectangle r)
        {
            return new Rectangle { X = r.X, Y = r.Y, Width = r.Width, Height = r.Height, Color = r.Color };
        }
        throw new ArgumentException("Unknown shape type");
    }
}
```

```typescript
class Circle {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  radius: number;
  color: string;
  private internalId: string;  // Private field!

  constructor(x: number, y: number, radius: number, color: string) {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
    this.radius = radius;
    this.color = color;
    this.internalId = crypto.randomUUID();
  }
}

class Rectangle {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  color: string;
  private internalId: string;  // Private field!

  constructor(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, color: string) {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
    this.width = width;
    this.height = height;
    this.color = color;
    this.internalId = crypto.randomUUID();
  }
}

// Must know the concrete type!
function copyShape(shape: Circle | Rectangle): Circle | Rectangle {
  if (shape instanceof Circle) {
    // Must know all fields
    return new Circle(shape.x, shape.y, shape.radius, shape.color);
    // Can't copy internalId - it's private!
  }
  if (shape instanceof Rectangle) {
    return new Rectangle(shape.x, shape.y, shape.width, shape.height, shape.color);
  }
  throw new Error("Unknown shape type");
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
use std::any::Any;

mod shapes {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

    fn next_id() -> u64 {
        static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
        NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    pub struct Circle {
        pub x: i32,
        pub y: i32,
        pub radius: i32,
        pub color: String,
        internal_id: u64, // Private field!
    }

    impl Circle {
        pub fn new(x: i32, y: i32, radius: i32, color: &str) -> Self {
            Self {
                x,
                y,
                radius,
                color: color.to_string(),
                internal_id: next_id(),
            }
        }
    }

    pub struct Rectangle {
        pub x: i32,
        pub y: i32,
        pub width: i32,
        pub height: i32,
        pub color: String,
        internal_id: u64, // Private field!
    }

    impl Rectangle {
        pub fn new(x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, color: &str) -> Self {
            Self {
                x,
                y,
                width,
                height,
                color: color.to_string(),
                internal_id: next_id(),
            }
        }
    }
}

use shapes::{Circle, Rectangle};

fn copy_shape(shape: &dyn Any) -> Box<dyn Any> {
    // Must know the concrete type!
    if let Some(c) = shape.downcast_ref::<Circle>() {
        // Must know all fields; can't copy internal_id - it's private to `shapes`!
        Box::new(Circle::new(c.x, c.y, c.radius, &c.color))
    } else if let Some(r) = shape.downcast_ref::<Rectangle>() {
        Box::new(Rectangle::new(r.x, r.y, r.width, r.height, &r.color))
    } else {
        panic!("Unknown shape type")
    }
}
```

## Solution

The Prototype pattern solves this by:

1. Defining a `clone()` method in the base class/interface
2. Each concrete class implements `clone()` to copy itself
3. Client code calls `clone()` without knowing the concrete type

### UML Diagram

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class Shape {
        <<abstract>>
        +x: int
        +y: int
        +color: string
        +clone() Shape
    }

    class Circle {
        +radius: int
        +clone() Shape
    }

    class Rectangle {
        +width: int
        +height: int
        +clone() Shape
    }

    Shape <|-- Circle
    Shape <|-- Rectangle

    Circle ..> Circle : clones
    Rectangle ..> Rectangle : clones
```

### Refactored Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import copy

# Prototype Interface
class Shape(ABC):
    def __init__(self, x: int = 0, y: int = 0, color: str = "white"):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.color = color

    @abstractmethod
    def clone(self) -> "Shape":
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        pass

# Concrete Prototype
class Circle(Shape):
    def __init__(self, x: int = 0, y: int = 0, color: str = "white", radius: int = 0):
        super().__init__(x, y, color)
        self.radius = radius
        self._internal_id = id(self)  # Private field - still gets cloned!

    def clone(self) -> "Circle":
        # Deep copy handles all fields including private ones
        return copy.deepcopy(self)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"Circle(x={self.x}, y={self.y}, radius={self.radius}, color={self.color})"

# Concrete Prototype
class Rectangle(Shape):
    def __init__(self, x: int = 0, y: int = 0, color: str = "white", width: int = 0, height: int = 0):
        super().__init__(x, y, color)
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self._internal_id = id(self)

    def clone(self) -> "Rectangle":
        return copy.deepcopy(self)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"Rectangle(x={self.x}, y={self.y}, {self.width}x{self.height}, color={self.color})"
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
// Prototype Interface
public abstract class Shape : ICloneable
{
    public int X { get; set; }
    public int Y { get; set; }
    public string Color { get; set; } = "white";

    public abstract Shape Clone();

    // Explicit interface implementation
    object ICloneable.Clone() => Clone();
}

// Concrete Prototype
public class Circle : Shape
{
    public int Radius { get; set; }
    private readonly Guid _internalId = Guid.NewGuid();  // Private field - still gets cloned!

    public override Shape Clone()
    {
        // MemberwiseClone handles all fields including private ones
        return (Circle)MemberwiseClone();
    }

    public override string ToString()
        => $"Circle(x={X}, y={Y}, radius={Radius}, color={Color})";
}

// Concrete Prototype
public class Rectangle : Shape
{
    public int Width { get; set; }
    public int Height { get; set; }
    private readonly Guid _internalId = Guid.NewGuid();

    public override Shape Clone()
    {
        return (Rectangle)MemberwiseClone();
    }

    public override string ToString()
        => $"Rectangle(x={X}, y={Y}, {Width}x{Height}, color={Color})";
}
```

#### `TypeScript`

```typescript
// Prototype Interface
abstract class Shape {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  color: string;

  constructor(x: number = 0, y: number = 0, color: string = "white") {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
    this.color = color;
  }

  abstract clone(): Shape;
}

// Concrete Prototype
class Circle extends Shape {
  radius: number;
  private internalId: string;  // Private field - still gets cloned!

  constructor(x: number = 0, y: number = 0, color: string = "white", radius: number = 0) {
    super(x, y, color);
    this.radius = radius;
    this.internalId = crypto.randomUUID();
  }

  clone(): Circle {
    const cloned = new Circle(this.x, this.y, this.color, this.radius);
    // Copy private field explicitly if needed
    return cloned;
  }

  toString(): string {
    return `Circle(x=${this.x}, y=${this.y}, radius=${this.radius}, color=${this.color})`;
  }
}

// Concrete Prototype
class Rectangle extends Shape {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  private internalId: string;

  constructor(x: number = 0, y: number = 0, color: string = "white", width: number = 0, height: number = 0) {
    super(x, y, color);
    this.width = width;
    this.height = height;
    this.internalId = crypto.randomUUID();
  }

  clone(): Rectangle {
    return new Rectangle(this.x, this.y, this.color, this.width, this.height);
  }

  toString(): string {
    return `Rectangle(x=${this.x}, y=${this.y}, ${this.width}x${this.height}, color=${this.color})`;
  }
}
```

#### `Dart`

```dart
// Prototype Interface
abstract class Shape {
  int x;
  int y;
  String color;

  Shape({this.x = 0, this.y = 0, this.color = "white"});

  Shape clone();
}

// Concrete Prototype
class Circle extends Shape {
  int radius;
  final String _internalId;  // Private field - still gets cloned!

  Circle({super.x, super.y, super.color, this.radius = 0})
      : _internalId = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString();

  // Private constructor for cloning
  Circle._clone({
    required int x,
    required int y,
    required String color,
    required this.radius,
    required String internalId,
  }) : _internalId = internalId, super(x: x, y: y, color: color);

  @override
  Circle clone() {
    return Circle._clone(
      x: x,
      y: y,
      color: color,
      radius: radius,
      internalId: _internalId,
    );
  }

  @override
  String toString() => "Circle(x=$x, y=$y, radius=$radius, color=$color)";
}

// Concrete Prototype
class Rectangle extends Shape {
  int width;
  int height;
  final String _internalId;

  Rectangle({super.x, super.y, super.color, this.width = 0, this.height = 0})
      : _internalId = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString();

  Rectangle._clone({
    required int x,
    required int y,
    required String color,
    required this.width,
    required this.height,
    required String internalId,
  }) : _internalId = internalId, super(x: x, y: y, color: color);

  @override
  Rectangle clone() {
    return Rectangle._clone(
      x: x,
      y: y,
      color: color,
      width: width,
      height: height,
      internalId: _internalId,
    );
  }

  @override
  String toString() => "Rectangle(x=$x, y=$y, ${width}x$height, color=$color)";
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
use std::fmt;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

fn next_id() -> u64 {
    static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
    NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
}

// Prototype interface → a trait. `Clone` cannot be called through `dyn`
// (it returns `Self`, whose size is unknown), so each shape clones into a Box.
trait Shape: fmt::Display {
    fn clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Shape>;
}

// Concrete Prototype → `#[derive(Clone)]` writes the field-by-field copy
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Circle {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    color: String,
    radius: i32,
    internal_id: u64, // Private outside this module - still gets cloned!
}

impl Circle {
    fn new(x: i32, y: i32, color: &str, radius: i32) -> Self {
        Self {
            x,
            y,
            color: color.to_string(),
            radius,
            internal_id: next_id(),
        }
    }
}

impl Shape for Circle {
    fn clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Shape> {
        Box::new(self.clone())
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Circle {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "Circle(x={}, y={}, radius={}, color={})",
            self.x, self.y, self.radius, self.color
        )
    }
}

// Concrete Prototype
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Rectangle {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    color: String,
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    internal_id: u64,
}

impl Rectangle {
    fn new(x: i32, y: i32, color: &str, width: i32, height: i32) -> Self {
        Self {
            x,
            y,
            color: color.to_string(),
            width,
            height,
            internal_id: next_id(),
        }
    }
}

impl Shape for Rectangle {
    fn clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Shape> {
        Box::new(self.clone())
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Rectangle {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "Rectangle(x={}, y={}, {}x{}, color={})",
            self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height, self.color
        )
    }
}
```

:::

#### Usage

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Create original shapes
circle = Circle(10, 20, "red", 50)
rectangle = Rectangle(0, 0, "blue", 100, 50)

# Clone without knowing concrete type!
def duplicate_shape(shape: Shape) -> Shape:
    return shape.clone()

# Clone and modify
circle_copy = circle.clone()
circle_copy.x = 100  # Move the copy
circle_copy.color = "green"

print(f"Original: {circle}")    # Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
print(f"Copy: {circle_copy}")   # Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

# Works with any shape
shapes: list[Shape] = [circle, rectangle]
copies = [s.clone() for s in shapes]
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
// Create original shapes
var circle = new Circle { X = 10, Y = 20, Color = "red", Radius = 50 };
var rectangle = new Rectangle { X = 0, Y = 0, Color = "blue", Width = 100, Height = 50 };

// Clone without knowing concrete type!
Shape DuplicateShape(Shape shape) => shape.Clone();

// Clone and modify
var circleCopy = (Circle)circle.Clone();
circleCopy.X = 100;  // Move the copy
circleCopy.Color = "green";

Console.WriteLine($"Original: {circle}");   // Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
Console.WriteLine($"Copy: {circleCopy}");   // Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

// Works with any shape
var shapes = new List<Shape> { circle, rectangle };
var copies = shapes.Select(s => s.Clone()).ToList();
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
// Clone without knowing concrete type!
fn duplicate_shape(shape: &dyn Shape) -> Box<dyn Shape> {
    shape.clone_box()
}

fn main() {
    // Create original shapes
    let circle = Circle::new(10, 20, "red", 50);
    let rectangle = Rectangle::new(0, 0, "blue", 100, 50);

    // Clone and modify (the concrete type is known here, so plain `clone()` works)
    let mut circle_copy = circle.clone();
    circle_copy.x = 100; // Move the copy
    circle_copy.color = "green".to_string();
    println!("Original: {circle}"); // Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
    println!("Copy: {circle_copy}"); // Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

    // Works with any shape
    let shapes: Vec<Box<dyn Shape>> = vec![Box::new(circle), Box::new(rectangle)];
    let copies: Vec<Box<dyn Shape>> = shapes.iter().map(|s| duplicate_shape(s.as_ref())).collect();
}
```

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="🦀 Rust lens"}
| GoF role | Rust |
|---|---|
| Prototype interface | `trait Shape: Display` with `fn clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Shape>` |
| Concrete prototype | `#[derive(Clone)] struct Circle` + `impl Shape for Circle` |
| `clone()` body | `Box::new(self.clone())`: the derived `Clone` copies every field, private ones too |
| Shared base fields (`x`, `y`, `color`) | repeated in each struct: a trait cannot hold fields |
| Clone through the interface | `shape.clone_box()` on a `&dyn Shape` |

**Ownership:** `Clone::clone` returns `Self`, and behind `dyn Shape` the size of `Self` is unknown, so `Clone` cannot be called on a trait object (it is not *dyn-compatible*). `clone_box` is the classic workaround: each type clones itself and boxes the result. The clone is a new owner and shares nothing with the original, unless a field is an `Rc` or `Arc`. See the [OOP Cheatsheet](../oop/oop-cheatsheet.qmd#rust) for the general mapping.
:::

## Modern Approach

The classic solution hand-writes `clone()` in every class. Modern languages generate it. Python dataclasses support `copy.replace()`, C# records support `with`, TypeScript copies plain data with object spread, and Rust derives `Clone` and copies with changes through struct update syntax (`..circle.clone()`). Each of these copies and modifies in one expression. Because the shapes become immutable values, a copy can never accidentally share changes with its original.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Verdict: 🟢 Replaces** — the language writes the clone for you, and immutable values make copy-and-modify safe. Dart is the exception: its `copyWith` is a convention you write yourself or generate.
:::

### Feature Map

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class Shape(ABC)` with abstract `clone()` | `@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class Shape`: nothing abstract left |
| `clone()` in every subclass via `copy.deepcopy(self)` | `copy.replace(shape, **changes)` (3.13), supported by every dataclass |
| Clone, then mutate: `circle_copy.x = 100` | Copy and modify in one call: `copy.replace(circle, x=100)` |
| Deep copy of nested mutable state | `copy.deepcopy()` (unchanged) |

#### `C#`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `abstract class Shape : ICloneable` with `Clone()` | `abstract record Shape`: the compiler writes the clone |
| `(Circle)MemberwiseClone()` in each subclass | `circle with { X = 100, Color = "green" }` |
| Cast after cloning: `(Circle)circle.Clone()` | No cast: `with` keeps the static type, and keeps the runtime type through a `Shape` reference |
| Mutable `{ get; set; }` properties | `{ get; init; }`: a copy can't be changed afterwards |

#### `TypeScript`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `abstract class Shape` with abstract `clone()` | `Circle` / `Rectangle` as plain data types with a `kind` tag |
| `new Circle(this.x, …)` inside each `clone()` | Object spread: `{ ...circle, x: 100 }` |
| `toString()` on each class | A `describe(shape)` function over the union |
| Deep copy of nested data | `structuredClone()`, which returns plain objects: class instances lose their methods |

#### `Dart`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `Shape clone()` | `Shape copyWith({int? x, int? y, String? color})` |
| `Circle._clone(...)` private constructor | Not needed: `copyWith` calls the public `const` constructor |
| Clone, then mutate: `circleCopy.x = 100` | `circle.copyWith(x: 100, color: "green")` on immutable values |
| Hand-written `clone()` per class | Hand-written `copyWith()` here; `freezed` generates it |

#### `Rust`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `trait Shape` with `clone_box(&self) -> Box<dyn Shape>` | nothing to write: `#[derive(Clone)]` on the data |
| Separate `Circle` / `Rectangle` structs, each repeating `x`, `y`, `color` | one `Shape` struct with the shared fields + `enum Kind` for the part that differs |
| Clone, then mutate: `circle_copy.x = 100` | Copy and modify in one expression: `Shape { x: 100, ..circle.clone() }` |
| `Box::new(self.clone())` in every `impl Shape` | unchanged where an open set of types still hides behind `dyn` |

:::

**Ecosystem:** in Dart, `freezed` generates `copyWith`, `==`, and `toString`. In TypeScript, Immer (`produce`) copies nested state while sharing unchanged parts. In Python, Pydantic models offer `model_copy(update=…)`. In Rust, `dyn-clone` generates the `clone_box` boilerplate for trait objects.

### Modern Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Python 3.13+ — frozen dataclasses + copy.replace()
import copy
from dataclasses import dataclass


# Prototype → an immutable dataclass: no clone() to write
@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Shape:
    x: int = 0
    y: int = 0
    color: str = "white"


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Circle(Shape):
    radius: int = 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"Circle(x={self.x}, y={self.y}, radius={self.radius}, color={self.color})"


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Rectangle(Shape):
    width: int = 0
    height: int = 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"Rectangle(x={self.x}, y={self.y}, {self.width}x{self.height}, color={self.color})"


# --- Usage ---
circle = Circle(x=10, y=20, color="red", radius=50)
rectangle = Rectangle(x=0, y=0, color="blue", width=100, height=50)

# Clone and modify in one step; the original is untouched
circle_copy = copy.replace(circle, x=100, color="green")
print(f"Original: {circle}")  # Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
print(f"Copy: {circle_copy}")  # Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

# Clone without knowing the concrete type: copy.replace() keeps it
shapes: list[Shape] = [circle, rectangle]
for shape in shapes:
    print(copy.replace(shape, color="black"))
# Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=black)
# Rectangle(x=0, y=0, 100x50, color=black)
```

```csharp
// C# 9+ / .NET 5+ — records + `with` expressions

// Prototype → an immutable record: the compiler writes the clone
public abstract record Shape
{
    public int X { get; init; }
    public int Y { get; init; }
    public string Color { get; init; } = "white";
}

public record Circle : Shape
{
    public int Radius { get; init; }

    public override string ToString() => $"Circle(x={X}, y={Y}, radius={Radius}, color={Color})";
}

public record Rectangle : Shape
{
    public int Width { get; init; }
    public int Height { get; init; }

    public override string ToString() => $"Rectangle(x={X}, y={Y}, {Width}x{Height}, color={Color})";
}

// --- Usage ---
var circle = new Circle { X = 10, Y = 20, Color = "red", Radius = 50 };
var rectangle = new Rectangle { X = 0, Y = 0, Color = "blue", Width = 100, Height = 50 };

// Clone and modify in one step; the original is untouched
var circleCopy = circle with { X = 100, Color = "green" };
Console.WriteLine($"Original: {circle}");  // Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
Console.WriteLine($"Copy: {circleCopy}");  // Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

// Clone without knowing the concrete type: `with` keeps the runtime type
List<Shape> shapes = [circle, rectangle];
foreach (var shape in shapes)
    Console.WriteLine(shape with { Color = "black" });
// Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=black)
// Rectangle(x=0, y=0, 100x50, color=black)
```

#### `TypeScript`

```typescript
// TypeScript 5.x — plain data types + object spread

// Prototype → plain immutable data; a tagged union replaces the class hierarchy
type Circle = {
  readonly kind: "circle";
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly color: string;
  readonly radius: number;
};

type Rectangle = {
  readonly kind: "rectangle";
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly color: string;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly height: number;
};

type Shape = Circle | Rectangle;

const describe = (s: Shape): string =>
  s.kind === "circle"
    ? `Circle(x=${s.x}, y=${s.y}, radius=${s.radius}, color=${s.color})`
    : `Rectangle(x=${s.x}, y=${s.y}, ${s.width}x${s.height}, color=${s.color})`;

// --- Usage ---
const circle: Circle = { kind: "circle", x: 10, y: 20, color: "red", radius: 50 };
const rectangle: Rectangle = { kind: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, color: "blue", width: 100, height: 50 };

// Clone and modify in one step; the original is untouched
const circleCopy: Circle = { ...circle, x: 100, color: "green" };
console.log(`Original: ${describe(circle)}`);  // Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
console.log(`Copy: ${describe(circleCopy)}`);  // Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

// Clone without knowing the concrete type: spread keeps the `kind` tag
const shapes: Shape[] = [circle, rectangle];
for (const shape of shapes) {
  console.log(describe({ ...shape, color: "black" }));
}
// Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=black)
// Rectangle(x=0, y=0, 100x50, color=black)

// Spread is shallow. structuredClone() copies nested data deeply, but it returns
// plain objects: a class instance comes back without its prototype or methods.
```

#### `Dart`

```dart
// Dart 3.x — immutable classes, const constructors, copyWith

// Prototype → immutable values; copyWith is clone-and-modify in one call
abstract class Shape {
  final int x;
  final int y;
  final String color;

  const Shape({this.x = 0, this.y = 0, this.color = "white"});

  // Callers can copy any Shape without knowing its concrete type
  Shape copyWith({int? x, int? y, String? color});
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final int radius;

  const Circle({super.x, super.y, super.color, this.radius = 0});

  // Hand-written here; `freezed` generates it in real projects
  @override
  Circle copyWith({int? x, int? y, String? color, int? radius}) => Circle(
        x: x ?? this.x,
        y: y ?? this.y,
        color: color ?? this.color,
        radius: radius ?? this.radius,
      );

  @override
  String toString() => "Circle(x=$x, y=$y, radius=$radius, color=$color)";
}

class Rectangle extends Shape {
  final int width;
  final int height;

  const Rectangle({super.x, super.y, super.color, this.width = 0, this.height = 0});

  @override
  Rectangle copyWith({int? x, int? y, String? color, int? width, int? height}) => Rectangle(
        x: x ?? this.x,
        y: y ?? this.y,
        color: color ?? this.color,
        width: width ?? this.width,
        height: height ?? this.height,
      );

  @override
  String toString() => "Rectangle(x=$x, y=$y, ${width}x$height, color=$color)";
}

// --- Usage ---
void main() {
  const circle = Circle(x: 10, y: 20, color: "red", radius: 50);
  const rectangle = Rectangle(x: 0, y: 0, color: "blue", width: 100, height: 50);

  // Clone and modify in one step; the original is untouched
  final circleCopy = circle.copyWith(x: 100, color: "green");
  print("Original: $circle");  // Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
  print("Copy: $circleCopy");  // Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

  // Clone without knowing the concrete type: the override keeps it
  final shapes = <Shape>[circle, rectangle];
  for (final shape in shapes) {
    print(shape.copyWith(color: "black"));
  }
  // Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=black)
  // Rectangle(x=0, y=0, 100x50, color=black)
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
// Rust 1.85+ (edition 2024) — #[derive(Clone)], struct update syntax, enum for the varying part
use std::fmt;

// The part that differs per shape → an enum
#[derive(Clone)]
enum Kind {
    Circle { radius: i32 },
    Rectangle { width: i32, height: i32 },
}

// Prototype → one struct with the shared fields: no clone() to write
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Shape {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    color: String,
    kind: Kind,
}

impl fmt::Display for Shape {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        let (x, y, color) = (self.x, self.y, &self.color);
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Circle { radius } => {
                write!(f, "Circle(x={x}, y={y}, radius={radius}, color={color})")
            }
            Kind::Rectangle { width, height } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "Rectangle(x={x}, y={y}, {width}x{height}, color={color})"
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

// --- Usage ---
fn main() {
    let circle = Shape {
        x: 10,
        y: 20,
        color: "red".to_string(),
        kind: Kind::Circle { radius: 50 },
    };
    let rectangle = Shape {
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        color: "blue".to_string(),
        kind: Kind::Rectangle {
            width: 100,
            height: 50,
        },
    };

    // Clone and modify in one step; the original is untouched
    let circle_copy = Shape {
        x: 100,
        color: "green".to_string(),
        ..circle.clone()
    };
    println!("Original: {circle}"); // Original: Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=red)
    println!("Copy: {circle_copy}"); // Copy: Circle(x=100, y=20, radius=50, color=green)

    // Clone without knowing the kind: the same update works on every Shape
    let shapes = [circle, rectangle];
    for shape in &shapes {
        let recolored = Shape {
            color: "black".to_string(),
            ..shape.clone()
        };
        println!("{recolored}");
    }
    // Circle(x=10, y=20, radius=50, color=black)
    // Rectangle(x=0, y=0, 100x50, color=black)
}
```

:::

### Classic or Modern?

| Prefer built-in copies when | Keep a hand-written `clone()` when |
|---|---|
| Objects are values that you replace rather than mutate | The copy needs custom rules: a fresh ID, reset counters, shared vs. copied resources |
| You want to clone and modify in one expression | The object owns handles (files, sockets, locks) that must not be duplicated |
| Types are already records, dataclasses, or plain data | The object is a mutable entity whose identity matters, such as one that must register itself on creation |
| Rust: the set of shapes is closed, so one struct plus an `enum Kind` lets `..shape.clone()` work for all of them | Rust: shapes are an open set behind `Box<dyn Shape>`. `Clone` is not dyn-compatible, so keep `clone_box()` |

## Summary

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" collapse="false"}
**Prototype** creates new objects by cloning existing ones, letting you copy objects without coupling to their concrete classes.
:::

### Key Benefits

- **Independence from Concrete Classes**: Clone via interface without knowing the actual type
- **Avoid Expensive Initialization**: Skip costly setup by copying pre-configured objects
- **Copy Private State**: The object can copy its own private fields
- **Simpler Than Subclassing**: Create variants by cloning and modifying instead of creating subclasses

### When to Use

| ✅ Use When | ❌ Avoid When |
|------------|--------------|
| Creating objects is expensive (DB calls, file loading) | Objects are simple and cheap to create |
| You need copies with slight modifications | Each instance needs unique initialization |
| You want to reduce subclasses for object variants | Objects have circular references (complex deep copy) |
| Client shouldn't depend on concrete classes | |
